comment: Plain-language definitions for terms used in the wiring views. One line each; the wiring view links these terms in place and shows the definition without leaving the page.

terms.AWG: American Wire Gauge, the sizing system for wire thickness — lower number, thicker wire.
terms.BEC: Battery eliminator circuit: a regulator (often built into an ESC) that makes a lower voltage for the electronics from the main battery.
terms.CSI: Camera Serial Interface: the flat ribbon-cable link between a Raspberry Pi and its camera; it carries power and image data.
terms.ESC: Electronic speed controller: the driver board between the battery and a brushless motor; it sequences power to the motor's phases.
terms.I2C: A two-wire data bus (clock + data) for short hops between chips and sensors on the same robot.
terms.LiPo: Lithium-polymer battery: light and powerful, the common robot pack. '4S' on a label means four cells in series, about 14.8 V.
terms.PDB: Power distribution board: the board that splits the battery connection out to the ESCs and the rest of the robot.
terms.PWM: Pulse-width modulation: power switched on and off very fast, and the fraction of 'on' time sets the average — how drivers meter motor power.
terms.TTL: Here, the Dynamixel serial signalling: the 3-wire chain (power, ground, data) that the servos share on one bus.
terms.ampacity: How much current a wire can carry safely before it overheats — thicker wire (a lower AWG number) means more ampacity.
terms.buck converter: A regulator that steps a higher voltage down to a lower one efficiently — 11.1 V battery to 5 V logic, in these robots.
terms.bus: A shared set of wires several parts connect to, carrying power, data, or both — parts share it instead of each getting a private line.
terms.connector: The plug pair at a cable's ends (XT60, JST, …): it sets how the cable attaches and how much current it may carry.
terms.current: Electrical flow, in amps (A): how much charge per second a wire or part is carrying.
terms.daisy chain: Wiring parts one after another along the same cable — servo 2 plugs into servo 1 — instead of a separate cable home for every part.
terms.encoder: A sensor that counts a motor shaft's rotation, so the controller knows how far and fast a wheel or joint actually turned.
terms.flight controller: The drone's autopilot board: reads the IMU, runs the stabilization math and commands the ESCs, hundreds of times a second.
terms.gauge: Wire thickness, measured in AWG: the lower the number, the thicker the wire and the more current it can carry.
terms.harness: The robot's whole set of cables, made and routed as one assembly — unplug the harness and the electronics come apart.
terms.microcontroller: A small, cheap computer-on-a-chip (Arduino-class): runs one program and talks directly to motors and sensors.
terms.rail: A wire (or board trace) that carries one steady voltage to several parts — 'the 5 V rail' is the shared 5 V supply line.
terms.regulator: A part that converts one voltage into another steady one — battery 11.1 V down to the clean 5 V a computer wants, for example.
terms.servo: A motor with its own controller and position sensor in one package: you command an angle and it holds it.
terms.stall torque: The most twisting force a motor can make while held still — the headline strength number for servos and gearmotors.
terms.voltage: Electrical pressure, in volts (V). A part's rated voltage is what it is built to run on; much more can destroy it.
